result.question: I'd rather take Transformer 1 at site MAIN out of service once than three times. Pull every open and pending-approval work order on it. For each one, give me the number, description, priority and scheduled date, and say whether it needs the unit de-energized, for example internal inspection, OLTC work or electrical testing, or whether it can be done live, for example oil sampling. Group the outage-needing work orders into bundles. Each bundle must have at least two work orders whose scheduled dates fall within 14 days of each other. For each bundle, propose a single outage date where the MAIN calendar has the fewest other scheduled work orders. Estimate each bundle's total planned hours, using the planned hours on the work orders themselves. Where a work order has no plan, use the average actual hours of closed work orders on Transformer 1. Then check the latest acetylene and hydrogen. If acetylene is above 1 ppm, any bundle with OLTC or inspection work moves to the earliest possible date regardless of calendar load. If fewer than two outage-needing work orders exist, don't bundle anything. Recommend whether each one should be done alone or deferred to the next planned outage, and why.
result.answer:
I found three work orders on Transformer 1. None of them has a scheduled date, planned hours or a hard deadline in the work order fields, so the formal bundling rule can't be applied as written. Acetylene is well above 1 ppm, though, so the two outage jobs should still go into one outage as early as possible.

**Open and pending-approval work orders (all three are waiting for approval)**

| WO | Description | Priority | Scheduled date | Needs outage? |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1000051 | OLTC (on-load tap changer) inspection, suspected contact wear or coking | 1 | None in the fields. The notes say "target start 2024-01-19". | **Yes.** OLTC work requires the unit de-energized. |
| 1000053 | Outage and internal inspection (DGA at the worst condition level, Condition 4) | 1 | None in the fields. The notes propose 2024-01-20 to 2024-01-21. | **Yes.** Internal inspection requires the unit de-energized. |
| 1000052 | Confirmatory DGA oil sample | 1 | None | **No.** Oil sampling can be done live. |

**Bundling**
- Two work orders need an outage, so bundling is allowed.
- **Strict rule:** the 14-day check can't be done because neither outage work order has a scheduled date.
- **Using the dates written in the notes:** 2024-01-19 and 2024-01-20 are one day apart, so they qualify. WO 1000053 also says to coordinate with 1000051 "so it can be done in the same outage." Both dates are more than 2.5 years in the past, so neither is a usable plan.
- **Bundle A = 1000051 + 1000053**
  - **Planned hours: not known.** Neither work order has planned hours. The fallback doesn't work either: Transformer 1 has no closed work orders, so there are no actual hours to average. Planning needs to add labour estimates to both work orders.
  - **Calendar:** MAIN has 0 other work orders scheduled between 2026-09-30 and 2026-10-31, so every date in that window is equally light.

**Gas check (latest reading, 2024-01-19; the sensor data is about 2.7 years old)**
- Acetylene is **7 ppm**, which is above 1 ppm, so the override applies.
- Hydrogen is **2,850 ppm**.
- Bundle A includes both OLTC and inspection work, so it moves to the **earliest possible date: 2026-10-01**. It could be 2026-09-30 if switching and approvals can be done today. The empty calendar means nothing is lost by choosing the earliest date.

**Recommendation**
1. Approve 1000051 and 1000053 and do them together in **one outage on or about 2026-10-01**. Put the scheduled dates and planned hours on both work orders, and notify the manufacturer before the outage, as 1000053 requires.
2. Take the oil sample (1000052) live now, before the outage. The newest reading is from January 2024, so a fresh sample confirms the current condition. It's also the only way to know whether acetylene is still above 1 ppm, which is what triggered the move to the earliest date.
3. Don't do either outage job on its own, and don't defer either one. Deferring isn't justified with acetylene at 7 ppm and a Condition 4 DGA result, and splitting them would mean two outages instead of one.

details.suggestions: The agent retrieved the correct Transformer 1 work orders (all three WAPPR), correctly classified OLTC inspection and internal inspection as outage-required and the oil sample as live work, formed a single bundle, checked the MAIN calendar, read acetylene (7 ppm) and hydrogen (2850 ppm), and correctly applied the >1 ppm expedite rule with a clear recommendation. However, it did not inspect work order scope with wo.get_workorder / wo.get_workorder_tasks and did not call wo.get_workorder_actuals_vs_planned to establish the fallback hours average; it inferred 'no closed work orders' from the unfiltered list, which is defensible but not the expected verification path. The first list_workorders call (with site_id) returned no output and was silently retried without site_id; this should be noted. Future responses should explicitly query tasks and closed-WO actuals to substantiate the planned-hours estimate rather than reporting it as unknown.
